variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: The GenAI system design interview framework is a seven-step method for turning an open-ended generative AI prompt into a complete production design. It moves from requirements gathering and ML framing through data, model architecture, evaluation, system architecture, deployment, and monitoring.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “The seven-step GenAI interview framework”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Clarify the product contract
pairs.detail: Define users, tasks, modalities, latency, risk, privacy, volume, and explicit non-goals.
pairs.explanation: Define users, tasks, modalities, latency, risk, privacy, volume, and explicit non-goals.

pairs.label: Frame the ML behavior
pairs.detail: Name inputs, outputs, acceptable uncertainty, retrieval or generation needs, and success criteria.
pairs.explanation: Name inputs, outputs, acceptable uncertainty, retrieval or generation needs, and success criteria.

pairs.label: Design data and evidence
pairs.detail: Specify sources, permissions, labeling, freshness, lineage, evaluation sets, and feedback capture.
pairs.explanation: Specify sources, permissions, labeling, freshness, lineage, evaluation sets, and feedback capture.

pairs.label: Select the model strategy
pairs.detail: Compare prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, tool use, and model tiers against measured constraints.
pairs.explanation: Compare prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, tool use, and model tiers against measured constraints.

pairs.label: Define evaluation and safety
pairs.detail: Combine deterministic checks, task metrics, calibrated judges, red teams, and human review.
pairs.explanation: Combine deterministic checks, task metrics, calibrated judges, red teams, and human review.

pairs.label: Draw the critical paths
pairs.detail: Separate synchronous response work from asynchronous ingestion, training, analytics, and feedback loops.
pairs.explanation: Separate synchronous response work from asynchronous ingestion, training, analytics, and feedback loops.

pairs.label: Operate and improve
pairs.detail: Plan deployment, monitoring, cost control, incident response, rollback, and evidence-driven iteration.
pairs.explanation: Plan deployment, monitoring, cost control, incident response, rollback, and evidence-driven iteration.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. Use the full lesson’s worked examples and interactive labs to explore the trade-offs behind these questions.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Clarify the product contract: Define users, tasks, modalities, latency, risk, privacy, volume, and explicit non-goals. Frame the ML behavior: Name inputs, outputs, acceptable uncertainty, retrieval or generation needs, and success criteria. Design data and evidence: Specify sources, permissions, labeling, freshness, lineage, evaluation sets, and feedback capture. Select the model strategy: Compare prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, tool use, and model tiers against measured constraints. Define evaluation and safety: Combine deterministic checks, task metrics, calibrated judges, red teams, and human review. Draw the critical paths: Separate synchronous response work from asynchronous ingestion, training, analytics, and feedback loops. Operate and improve: Plan deployment, monitoring, cost control, incident response, rollback, and evidence-driven iteration.

pairs.label: Safety and moderation
pairs.detail: Place deterministic authority and human escalation around probabilistic generation and tool use.
pairs.explanation: Place deterministic authority and human escalation around probabilistic generation and tool use.

pairs.label: Scale and economics
pairs.detail: Connect traffic and token estimates to batching, caching, capacity, fallbacks, and cost per successful outcome.
pairs.explanation: Connect traffic and token estimates to batching, caching, capacity, fallbacks, and cost per successful outcome.

variants.prompt: Why should a GenAI system design interview begin with the product contract rather than a model choice?
options: The contract exposes the users, task, risk, latency, privacy, scale, and non-goals that constrain later choices.
The model cannot be discussed until implementation is complete.
Every GenAI product ultimately uses the same architecture.
Product requirements replace the need for evaluation.
variants.explanation: Architecture is a response to constraints. Clarifying the product contract provides the evidence needed to defend data, model, serving, and control decisions.

variants.prompt: A candidate improves task success by 8 percentage points but produces one critical privacy leak in the release suite. What is the correct release decision?
options: Hold the release, repair the control, and rerun the release suite.
Average the privacy result into the quality score and launch if the total is positive.
Launch globally because task success improved.
Ignore the failure if cost per request decreased.
variants.explanation: Critical safety failures are separate hard gates. A quality or cost gain cannot compensate for a release-blocking harm.

variants.prompt: A support assistant must answer from records updated every minute and cite its evidence. Which design choice follows most directly?
options: Use live or near-live retrieval with freshness metadata and source citations.
Fine-tune once and remove retrieval to reduce complexity.
Cache every answer indefinitely.
Train a larger model and assume its internal knowledge remains current.
variants.explanation: Rapidly changing source facts require a fresh evidence path. Model size does not guarantee current knowledge or traceable citations.

variants.prompt: Offline quality, safety, and cost gates all pass. What rollout does that evidence justify first?
options: A bounded canary with monitored abort thresholds.
Immediate global exposure with no rollback plan.
Permanent shadow mode even after all gates pass.
Deletion of the control model so users cannot be split between variants.
variants.explanation: Offline evidence earns limited production exposure. A canary tests real traffic while limiting blast radius and preserving rollback.

variants.prompt: What changes when a generated response can execute a purchase instead of only displaying text?
options: Typed tools, least-privilege authorization, confirmation, and idempotent side-effect handling become part of the critical path.
Only the prompt wording needs to change.
Safety evaluation is no longer necessary because the tool has an API schema.
The model should receive unrestricted credentials to avoid latency.
variants.explanation: Tool use turns a generation error into a real side effect. Deterministic authorization and confirmation must surround the probabilistic model.

variants.prompt: Which metric best connects GenAI serving cost to actual product value?
options: Cost per successful task, measured with a defined success criterion.
Total token count without task outcomes.
Model parameter count alone.
The provider's maximum context window.
variants.explanation: Cost per successful task couples unit economics to an outcome. Raw token or parameter counts do not reveal whether the system delivered value.
